hook: Lysosomes refill their calcium through TMEM184 proteins, a long-missing transporter.
summary: A genetic screen of lysosomal membrane proteins found that TMEM184 proteins carry calcium into lysosomes, the uptake step that was previously unidentified. Losing TMEM184B and C emptied calcium stores and disrupted membrane repair and related functions, and a human mutation linked to a neurodevelopmental disorder impaired transport. Mice lacking Tmem184b had severe motor problems. The work is in cells and mice, so its relevance to human disease is inferred from one mutation.
title: TMEM184 proteins are Ca2+ uptake transporters in lysosomes.
